'''Edward William Abel''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|commas=on|CBE|FRSC}} (3 December 1931 – 19 April 2021)<ref>{{Cite web |title=ABEL - Deaths Announcements - Telegraph Announcements |url=http://announcements.telegraph.co.uk/deaths/249349/abel |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230417015616/http://announcements.telegraph.co.uk/deaths/249349/abel |archive-date=2023-04-17 |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=announcements.telegraph.co.uk |language=en}}</ref> was a British [[chemist]], editor of textbooks on [[organometallic chemistry]] and president of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (1996–1998).<ref name="whos who">{{cite book|title=The International Who's Who 2017|edition=80th|volume=1 (A-K)|date=2016|location=[[Abingdon-on-Thames|Abingdon, Oxfordshire]]|publisher=[[Routledge]]|isbn=978-1-85743-840-6 |url=https://archive.org/details/internationalwho0001unse|via=[[Internet Archive]]|page=5}}</ref>

==Early life and education ==
Abel was born in [[Kenfig Hill]], [[Bridgend County Borough]],<ref name=":3">{{Citation |title=The Presidents of the Chemical Society & Royal Society of Chemistry (1841–2024) |page=38 |url=https://www.rsc.org/getContentAsset/c8c542d6-3e85-42f6-ba12-c73a60602fdb/f4c91d86-ac3e-4675-bdf3-f8325ded9710/rsc-presidents-1841-2024.pdf |publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]}}</ref> the son of Sidney John Abel and Donna Maria (née Grabham). He attended Bridgend County Grammar School, where he gained his [[Higher School Certificate (England and Wales)|Higher School Certificate]] in 1949.<ref name=":2">{{cite news|title=Kenfig Hill Man's Scholarship|newspaper=Glamorgan Gazette|page=4|date=21 September 1956}}</ref> Abel went on to study chemistry at [[University of Wales, Cardiff]], where he was an undergraduate student of [[John Howard Purnell|Professor Howard Purnell]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=John Meurig |author-link=John Meurig Thomas |date=1996-01-17 |title=OBITUARY: Professor Howard Purnell |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/obituary-professor-howard-purnell-1324382.html |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> Following his graduation from Cardiff, he served with the British Army during the [[Korean War]].<ref name="trager" /> He then pursued postgraduate studies at the [[University of North London|Northern Polytechnic]] (now part of [[London Metropolitan University]]), supported by a Postgraduate Research Scholarship from the Courtaulds' Scientific and Educational Trust Fund, awarded in 1956.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite journal |date=1956 |title=Courtaulds' Scientific and Educational Trust Fund: Postgraduate Research Scholarships for 1956 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/178622f0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=178 |issue=4534 |pages=622–623 |doi=10.1038/178622f0 |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Under the supervision of [[Michael F. Lappert]], Abel finished his PhD in just two years.<ref name="trager" />

==Academic career==
Following his PhD, Abel continued his research at [[Imperial College London]], working as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|post-doctoral research fellow]] in the laboratory of future [[List of Nobel laureates in Chemistry|Nobel laureate]] [[Geoffrey Wilkinson]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Kenfig Hill Man's Degree|newspaper=Glamorgan Gazette|page=1|date=18 October 1957}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Dunning |first=Hayley |date=2017-02-14 |title=Explosions, Nobel Prizes and poems: a history of the Department of Chemistry |url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/177516/explosions-nobel-prizes-poems-history-department/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=[[Imperial College London]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> In 1959, he joined [[University of Bristol]] as a lecturer<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1959-08-08 |title=University News |url=https://doi.org/10.1038/184410a0 |journal=Nature |volume=184 |issue=4684 |pages=410–410 |doi=10.1038/184410a0 |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and was later promoted to [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]].<ref name="whos who" /> In 1972, he became Professor of Inorganic Chemistry at [[University of Exeter]]. He was also Exeter's head of Chemistry from 1977 to 1988,<ref name="trager" /> and deputy-vice-chancellor from 1991 to 1994.<ref name="whos who" /><ref>{{Who's Who|title=Abel, Prof. Edward William|id=U4906|year=2021|type=was}}</ref> Among his doctoral students at Exeter was [[Suresh Bhargava]] {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AM|size=100%}}, now a Distinguished Professor of Chemistry who has enjoyed a successful career in Australia.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Long |first=Nicholas J. |last2=Bhargava |first2=Suresh |date=2022 |title=Professor Edward Abel, FRSC, CBE (1931–2021) |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2022/dt/d2dt90160a |journal=Dalton Transactions |language=en |volume=51 |issue=44 |pages=16781–16783 |doi=10.1039/D2DT90160A|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Throughout Abel's career, he also held visiting positions at [[University of British Columbia]] (1970), [[TU Braunschweig]] (1973), and [[Australian National University]] (1990).<ref name="whos who" /> He served as President of the Royal Society of Chemistry from 1996 to 1998. Upon his retirement from Exeter in 1997, he was made [[Professor Emeritus]].<ref name=":3" />

=== Workplace incidents ===
In 1959 Abel was injured in an explosion at Imperial. "He received burns to his hands and cuts but his injuries [were] not thought to be serious"<ref>{{cite news|title=Man Injured in a Laboratory Blast|newspaper=Leicester Daily Mercury|page=9|date=2 February 1959}}</ref><ref name="trager">{{cite web|last=Trager|first=Rebecca|title=Former Royal Society of Chemistry president and organometallic chemist Eddie Abel dies|website=Chemistry World (RSC)|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/tributes-paid-as-royal-society-of-chemistry-past-president-eddie-abel-dies/4013586.article|date=26 April 2021|access-date=13 September 2025}}</ref> The explosion also blew off several windows as well as the door of Wilkinson's office, which was adjacent to Abel's lab.<ref name=":0" />

Abel collapsed at work during his time at Exeter, as recalled by his student Bhargava. He was hospitalised following the incident but soon recovered.<ref name=":1" />

=== Honours and recognitions ===
Abel was a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name=":1" /> He won the society's [[Tilden Prize]] for outstanding contributions to chemistry research in the 1980/81 academic year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tilden Prizes for Chemistry |url=https://www.rsc.org/standards-and-recognition/prizes/research-and-innovation-prizes/tilden-prize-for-chemistry |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Royal Society of Chemistry |language=en}}</ref>

He was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[1997 Birthday Honours|1997 Queen's Birthday Honours]], for services to chemistry.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=54794|date=14 June 1997|supp=1|page=7}}</ref> In 2000, he was awarded an [[Honorary degree|honorary]] [[Doctor of Science]] degree from [[University of Exeter]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Previous honorary graduates |url=https://www.exeter.ac.uk/about/honorarygraduates/archive/previous/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=[[University of Exeter]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Abel married Margaret Rosina Edwards in Bridgend on 6 August 1960. They had a son and a daughter: Edward Christopher (1963) and Julia Margaret (1967) who, between them, have four grandchildren.<ref name="funeral">{{cite web|title=The obituary notice of Professor Edward William ABEL|website=Funeral Notices|url=https://funeral-notices.co.uk/notice/abel/4941305|access-date=13 September 2025}}</ref> Margaret Rosina Abel died on 4 February 2018. Eddie Abel died in [[Cobham, Surrey|Cobham]] on 19 April 2021.<ref name=":1" /> His funeral was held at Randall's Park Crematorium, [[Leatherhead]] on 18 May 2021.<ref name="funeral" />
